subject: Pinecrest RFI: data territory, retention and erase workflow (hosted API)
messages:
From: Laura McBride <laura.mcbride@pinecresthealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Grant <tim.grant@pinecresthealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-23T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Data residency and deletion—hosted API (RFI)

Ben —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we move to procurement we need a short RFI to clear our security review. Can you confirm the hosted API behavior for the items below? A concise written response for each point is perfect — we will include your answers in our vendor pack.

1) Data residency: if we choose the US region, exactly which AWS region(s) do you use for production data and backups? Do you provide region pinning per tenant, and is metadata (request timestamps, tenant id) stored outside the chosen region?

2) Retention windows: what are your default retention windows for (a) request/response payloads, (b) tokenized model inputs/outputs (if stored separately), (c) logs/traces used for debugging? Can we request a custom retention (e.g., 0 days or 7 days) for our account on hosted? Any costs or contract implications?

3) Deletion/erase process: describe the steps and expected timelines when Pinecrest requests a full data purge: immediate deletion from active stores, backup lifecycle, evidence of deletion, and third-party snapshot copies. We need a rough SLA for complete removal from your systems.

4) Backups and disaster recovery: how long are backups retained, are they geo-replicated, and how are they handled during an erase request?

5) Key management: do you use provider-managed keys or offer BYOK (customer-managed keys) for the hosted API? If BYOK is available, where are keys stored and who controls rotation?

6) Legal hold / subpoenas: how are requests for legal hold handled, and will that pause scheduled erasures for customer accounts?

7) Evidence and audit: what artifacts can you provide to demonstrate retention/deletion (deletion receipts, audit logs, snapshots)? Are those available in the Console or via a security evidence package?

We appreciate a response by COB tomorrow if possible. Attach any short artifacts (one-pagers, playbook) that will help our security team.

—Laura
Laura McBride
Head of Security Operations

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Laura McBride <laura.mcbride@pinecresthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data residency and deletion—hosted API (RFI)

Hi Laura — thanks for the RFI. Below are concise, actionable answers mapped to your numbered questions. Where appropriate I note exceptions for Dedicated/Private deployments.

1) Data residency
- Production active data: for US-hosted tenants we operate primarily in us-east-1 and us-west-2 depending on capacity and routing policy. Customers can request pinning to a single region at account onboarding; we document the chosen region in the Console and contract.
- Backups: snapshots are stored in the same region by default and are not replicated outside the region unless the customer enables cross-region replication for DR.
- Metadata: tenant identifiers and minimal routing metadata are stored in the control plane. For hosted API the control plane is multi-region; we replicate control-plane metadata (tenant ID, routing preference) in a limited set of regions for high availability. We do not store request/response payloads in regions outside the pinned data region except for transient caches used in routing (these are purged within minutes).

2) Retention windows
- Request/response payloads: default retention is 14 days in the hosted API offering (this includes request text and generated outputs).
- Tokenized inputs/outputs / model caches: we retain model-level caches (KV caches) only for active sessions; persisted token artifacts (used for safety or quality monitoring) are retained under the same 14-day window unless explicitly configured otherwise.
- Logs/traces: operational logs and traces that support debugging and SLOs are retained for 90 days by default (searchable in Console).
- Custom retention: we offer account-level retention adjustments on hosted API (options: 0 days (ephemeral), 7 days, 14 days, 30 days). A 0-day setting means we do not persist payloads beyond the immediate inference pipeline; limited diagnostic logs (no payload) are retained per our operational needs. Shorter retention tiers are available via a contractual addendum; 0-day requests require a minimum security addendum and may affect our ability to provide deep debugging support.

3) Deletion / erase process and timelines
- Active store purge: when Pinecrest requests a full purge we remove tenant payloads from primary storage and caches within 48 hours.
- Backups and snapshots: deletion from backups is performed on the next backup lifecycle; for practical purposes full removal from standard backups can take up to 90 days (typical retention + backup rotation). We provide an accelerated purge option in commercial contracts (SLA: complete removal from backups within 30 days) as an add-on.
- Evidence: after the purge we provide a deletion confirmation (signed receipt) and a summary audit report showing object identifiers, timestamps, and the purge workflow steps performed.
- Third-party snapshots: we maintain inventories of export locations and third-party snapshots and coordinate deletion where Redwood controls the snapshot. For any copies held by third-party providers under subprocessor arrangements we include evidence of Redwood's deletion request; third-party times vary and are documented in our subprocessor list.

4) Backups and disaster recovery
- Default retention windows for backups align with our standard DR policy (90 days for snapshot metadata; payloads follow account retention). Backups are stored in-region by default.
- Geo-replication is off by default for privacy-conscious customers; enabled only if configured for DR and documented in the agreement.
- On erase requests we invalidate affected snapshots and mark them for deletion; deletion completes according to the backup rotation SLA described above.

5) Key management
- Hosted API: we use provider-managed master keys by default.
- BYOK: customer-managed keys are available as an enterprise option for hosted customers who require it. With BYOK keys are stored in the customer's KMS account (we support AWS KMS CMKs with a cross-account grant model) or in an HSM-backed service depending on customer preference. Key rotation is customer-controlled when BYOK is enabled; Redwood personnel do not have access to the plaintext key material.

6) Legal hold / subpoenas
- If a valid legal hold or subpoena is served for a tenant, Redwood will preserve the requested data and pause scheduled erasure for the scope and duration of the hold. We notify customers of legal process affecting their account where legally permitted and record holds in the audit trail. Holds are reflected in our Console and in the deletion/audit reports.

7) Evidence and audit
- Artifacts we provide: deletion receipts (signed PDF), audit log extract for the affected tenant (object ids, actions, actor), and a short playbook PDF that explains the purge workflow.
- Delivery: evidence packages are delivered via a secure share link and can be made available through the Console or via our security evidence pack on request. For procurement we can provide a one-time evidence bundle (zip) containing the above.

Notes / caveats
- SLA exceptions: accelerated backup purge and BYOK are available under an enterprise contract and may require minimum term.
- For the strictest data residency controls (no control-plane replication of tenant identifiers), we recommend Redwood Private or a Dedicated deployment; we can outline a migration path if Pinecrest prefers that model.

Attachments: final answers spreadsheet and a short hosted-erase-playbook PDF included with this reply.

If you want a single-line summary for the vendor pack: "Hosted API stores payloads in the customer-chosen region, default payload retention 14 days, active-store purge within 48 hours, full backup removal typically within 90 days (30-day accelerated option available). BYOK and enterprise retention exceptions available by contract."

Happy to expand any section or provide a redlined addendum for procurement.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
